THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA, PRAYING TO DECLARE THAT THE ACQUISITION PROCEEDINGS PERTAINING TO THE SCHEDULED PROPERTY IN PURSUANCE OF FINAL NOTIFICATION DATED 7.5.2007 ISSUED BY THE R2 A COPY OF WHICH IS PRODUCED AT ANNEXURE-B IS DEEMED TO HAVE BEEN LAPSED SO FAR AS PETITIONERS IS CONCERNED AND ETC.,
 THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING,
THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

Petitioner - lady is knocking at the doors of Writ Court for laying a challenge to the acquisition of land pursuant to Final Notification dated 07.05.2007 made under the provisions of Section 28(4) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner vehemently argues that till date the possession of the land remains with his client and therefore, she is entitled to protection under Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He also draws attention of the Court to certain photographs at Annexure-A Series to adumbrate his stand that his client is still in the possession & cultivation of the subject land.

sentences.text: After service of notice, the 1st Respondent - State is represented by learned AGA and the Respondent - KIADB & its officials are represented by its learned Sr. Panel Counsel; the 4th Respondent - Company is represented by its private counsel.
All they oppose the Petition making submission in justification of the impugned acquisition proceedings.

Learned Sr. Panel Counsel appearing for the KIADB submits that the land having been acquired years ago, a sum of Rs.23.25,000/- has been credited to the Bank Account of the Petitioner on 21.07.2008 vide Cheque bearing NO. 0204166 dated 16.07.2008.
To substantiate the same, he has produced Statement of Account of the Corporation Bank, now Union Bank of India.

3. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition papers, this Court declines indulgence in the matter inasmuch as, the Scheme of acquisition envisaged under Section 28 of the 1966 Act contemplates vesting of land once the Final Notification is issued under Section 28(4) notwithstanding an award being passed or compensation being paid, vide Division Bench judgment in W.P.NO.17600/2004 ETC., BETWEEN NANDI INFRASTRUCTURE CORRIDOR ENTERPRISE LIMITED VS. STATE & OTHERS, disposed off on 15.06.2011.

entities.text: BETWEEN NANDI INFRASTRUCTURE CORRIDOR ENTERPRISE LIMITED VS. STATE & OTHERS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This apart, the acquisition is by agreement under Section 29(2) of the 1966 Act and therefore, the question of laying a challenge to the acquisition would not arise as held by this Court in a catena of decisions.

4. There is force in the submission of learned Panel Counsel that in light of Apex Court decision in SPECIAL LAND ACQUISITION OFFICER, KIADB & OTHERS vs. ANUSUYA BAI (D)BY LRS., 2017 3 SCC 313, the benefit of Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act does not avail to the owners of the land acquired under the statutes other than Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

entities.text: SPECIAL LAND ACQUISITION OFFICER, KIADB & OTHERS vs. ANUSUYA BAI (D)BY LRS., 2017 3 SCC 313
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He is also justified in telling that once the land is vested, persons continuing in theoccupation of the land are nothing but tresspassers of first order vide INDORE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY vs. MAHOHAR LAL, 2020 (8) SCC 129.

entities.text: INDORE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY vs. MAHOHAR LAL, 2020 (8) SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, the Writ Petition is liable to be disposed off and accordingly it is.
Liberty is reserved to the Petitioner to workout her remedy before the Hon'ble Lokayktha wherein proceedings are stated to be pending against the 4th Respondent - Company and others as well.
Nothing stated herein above would prejudice such proceedings.
No costs.

Petitioner - lady is knocking at the doors of Writ Court for laying a challenge to the acquisition of land pursuant to Final Notification dated 07.05.2007 made under the provisions of Section 28(4) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
3. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition papers, this Court declines indulgence in the matter inasmuch as, the Scheme of acquisition envisaged under Section 28 of the 1966 Act contemplates vesting of land once the Final Notification is issued under Section 28(4) notwithstanding an award being passed or compensation being paid, vide Division Bench judgment in W.P.NO.17600/2004 ETC., BETWEEN NANDI INFRASTRUCTURE CORRIDOR ENTERPRISE LIMITED VS. STATE & OTHERS, disposed off on 15.06.2011.
This apart, the acquisition is by agreement under Section 29(2) of the 1966 Act and therefore, the question of laying a challenge to the acquisition would not arise as held by this Court in a catena of decisions.
He is also justified in telling that once the land is vested, persons continuing in theoccupation of the land are nothing but tresspassers of first order vide INDORE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY vs. MAHOHAR LAL, 2020 (8) SCC 129.
